categories.label: Adaptive Flesh
description: An ongoing research exploring anatomical architectures designed for bodies in flux.

We no longer inhabit a singular, coherent reality.
Contemporary existence unfolds across overlapping experiences in digital, biological, syntethic environments.
Our perception of these realities frequently contradict one another, producing states of instability and cognitive dissonance - Adaptive Flesh emerges as a response to this condition.

This project explores how engineered morphologies can augment the body with integrated capacities for protection, calibration and resistance, functioning as adaptive interfaces between these changing landscapes.

Through a series of experimental artefacts, wearable structures, and material investigations, the aim of this research is to examine strategies of transformation and controlled adaptation, drawing inspiration from natural defense mechanisms and computational logic in technology.

projects.title: Transfiguration, 2026
projects.description: A sequence of developmental states compressed into a single organism, where emergence, decay, protection, and growth occur simultaneously. The surrounding membrane functions as a regulatory interface: a temporary structure that isolates the body from external pressures while allowing profound internal reorganization to take place. Within the framework of Adaptive Flesh, the chrysalis is understood not as a symbol of rebirth, but as a technology of adaptation — a protective system through which the body acquires the capacity to navigate changing realities.

projects.title: Pressure Calibration, 2026
projects.description: The project presents a speculative anatomical system designed to absorb, distribute, and regulate forces before they reach the surface. Inflated forms function as buffers between internal structures and external boundaries, selectively amplifying or suppressing what becomes visible. As part of Adaptive Flesh, this work proposes a system for the body as a calibration interface. The resulting morphology reflects not just the reality itself, but the conditions through which it is experienced.

projects.title: Force Matrix, 2026
projects.description: Explores the coexistence of protection and latent force within a single anatomical system. An external armor conceals an internal structure that is continuously present yet not visible at first sight. The work proposes that defense and offense are not opposites but reciprocal states of the same morphology. What protects also possesses the potential to act. What appears dormant retains the capacity for activation.

categories.label: Physical Works
description: Past traces emerges as “ghosts of intentions”, echoing through our present.

The remains, in this context, are imprints of desires and experiences hardened by time, yet never fully silent.
They speak to what once was, but also to what was meant to be or could still become.
An aesthetic of absence, delay and recurrence, where lost memories remain suspended in a perpetual state of becoming.
3D printed sculptural wearable in elastic TPU.

projects.title: Remains
projects.description:
“Remains” investigates the idea of the body through absence.
Emerging as a fossil-like fragment, this wearable evokes the imprint of a structure that once protected, supported, or transformed the organism that carried it.

Suspended between artifact and anatomy, the piece suggests that evolution leaves behind a residue through which its history can still be read.

paragraphs:
Sabrina Suppa is an artist and designer based in London. For the past five years, she has worked as a character artist in major studios within the gaming and film industries such as Framestore, DNEG, MPC and Ninja Theory, where she cultivated her fascination with anatomical studies and the expressive potential of the human body.
Alongside her work in the industry, in 2025 she began independently exploring 3D printing and physical fabrication as a personal pursuit, gradually shifting her practice towards a more intimate artistic language.

Defining herself as a Body Architect, Suppa’s work exists at the intersection of fashion, technology, and geometric abstraction, constructing conceptual structures that reshape and extend the human silhouette.
Influenced by an early background in Classical Piano and Interior Design, her work reflects a fascination with the body in its most unrestrained and transformative forms.

Through sculptural wearables and engineered morphologies, she explores ambivalence in perception: forms that mutate in meaning through subtraction or addition, objects that appear delicate or innocent while concealing latent force beneath their surface. Her practice investigates the tension between visibility and concealment, suggesting that what is hidden often carries the deepest resonance.
